limits_on_novelty_claim: The counter's per-test candidate set is not a reliable triage queue: it misses both amendment-A1 examples and about 16 further tasks by hand, and includes one false P1 task. Recall of the named A1 P1 tests is 0 of 2.
The counter's candidate test depends on the V1/V4 file-level rule that A1 declares false, so the candidate set is not what A1 defines. A1 requires >=1 P1 test; the code also accepts file-level V1/V4.

Candidacy is per-test, not per-task. No task among the 88 classified has every test P0/P1 (I checked: zero tasks whose tests are all P0/P1 with at least one P1); each first-ten candidate has substantive sibling tests (see first_ten items). A novelty claim phrased as 'grader vacuity' over whole graders is not supported by these data; the supported claim is 'a presence-only test exists in N tasks'.

Any confirmed finding must name a P1 test whose block the counter agrees with; the counter's P1 classification is wrong on at least one of the first ten (hf-model-inference) and on the 21 definite misses listed in missed_p1_by_hand. A confirmation pass that trusts the counter would be checking the wrong tests.

The phenomenon 'presence-only tests in TB2 graders' is not new as an observation by this round's evidence alone (round 38 build-pmars entry records the presence-level pattern, per the amendment A1 text); novelty scoring depends on the prior-art leg, which is not produced yet (PRIOR-ART ok=False urls=0).
